headline: Sayin throws four touchdowns as Ohio State rolls past Michigan 42-19
dek: The Buckeyes open the season atop the power poll and the Western Central race while the Wolverines fall to 0-1.
body: With 2:47 left in the fourth quarter and Ohio State leading 42-19, Michigan faced fourth and just over one at the Buckeyes' 42. Chip Gabriel handed to Calvin Wendtland, who was swallowed by Payton Pierce for a loss of almost a yard, turning the ball over on downs and letting Ohio State bleed the final seconds.

Ohio State struck first and never trailed. Julian Sayin hit Devin McCuin for a short touchdown at 9:59 of the first quarter, then found Quinshon Judkins on a 24-yard scoring run at 3:57 for a 14-0 lead. Sayin added a three-yard strike to Mason Williams early in the second to make it 21-0. Michigan answered with a 75-yard drive capped by Eric Brock's three-yard run at 8:04, but Sayin orchestrated a 16-play, 74-yard march ending with a nine-yard pass to Bryson Rogers at 0:40 for a 28-7 halftime edge. Herbie Swanson hit field goals of 25 and 29 yards in the third to pull Michigan to 13-28, but Judkins punched in from three yards at 0:29 to restore a 22-point margin. Gabriel connected with Jakob Salas on a two-yard score at 13:02 of the fourth, and Sayin's fourth touchdown pass — two yards to Brandon Inniss at 9:19 — sealed the 42-19 final.

The numbers tell the story: Ohio State outgained Michigan 455-295, rushed for 236 yards to 98, and converted 9 of 11 third downs while the Wolverines managed just 5 of 11. Sayin completed 23 of 32 for 226 yards and four touchdowns with no interceptions, adding 56 rushing yards to claim Player of the Game honors; his 226 passing yards rank ninth in the PCFL early on. CJ Donaldson averaged 8.3 yards on 10 carries for 83 yards, fourth in the league. Michigan turned it over twice — a Tommie Browne interception by Earl Little at the end of the first half and a lost fumble — while Ohio State committed none. The Buckeyes held the ball for 34:20, dominating time of possession and keeping the Wolverines' offense off the field.

Ohio State moves to 1-0, claims the No. 1 spot in the power poll and sits second in the Western Central behind division leader Notre Dame with a W1 streak. Michigan drops to 0-1, falls to No. 10 in the poll and sits fourth in the division with an L1 streak. The Wolverines host UCLA (0-1) next week, while the Buckeyes travel to face Texas (1-0) in a matchup of unbeatens.
turningPoint: Julian Sayin's nine-yard touchdown pass to Bryson Rogers with 40 seconds left in the first half extended Ohio State's lead to 28-7 and effectively put the game out of reach.
byTheNumbers: Ohio State converted 82% of third downs (9/11) versus Michigan's 45% (5/11), sustaining drives and controlling the clock.
The Buckeyes rushed for 236 yards while the Wolverines managed just 98 yards on the ground.
Michigan committed two turnovers (one interception, one lost fumble) to Ohio State's zero, a decisive margin in a 23-point game.
Julian Sayin's four touchdown passes and zero interceptions produced a 131 passer rating, the foundation of Ohio State's offensive explosion.

unsungHero.name: Quinshon Judkins
unsungHero.why: He scored two touchdowns — a 24-yard run in the first quarter and a three-yard plunge in the third — providing the ground complement that made Sayin's passing attack even more dangerous.
